forces.title: Geopolitical volatility and energy supply chain disruption risk.
forces.description: Ongoing geopolitical events, such as the conflict in West Asia, introduce significant volatility and risk to crude oil prices and global energy flows. This directly impacts integrated oil and gas companies, particularly Indian OMCs heavily reliant on imports. Such disruptions can rapidly increase feedstock costs, squeeze refining margins, and create challenges in maintaining consistent supply, thereby threatening financial stability and requiring agile sourcing strategies. This risk is compounded by India's high energy import dependency.

forces.title: Resilient global oil and gas demand growth through 2035.
forces.description: Despite decarbonization efforts, global oil demand is anticipated to remain resilient and even grow to 108 million barrels per day (Mb/d) by 2040 under some scenarios, and many industry executives expect peak oil demand in 2035 or later. This sustained demand, particularly for petrochemical feedstocks and heavy transport, provides a fundamental tailwind for integrated oil and gas companies, ensuring continued market for their core products and justifying ongoing investments in hydrocarbon assets.

forces.title: Government strategic investments boosting upstream E&P and gas sector.
forces.description: The Indian government is planning substantial investments, including US$348-406 billion by 2035 for upstream energy security and US$67 billion for the gas sector over 5-6 years. These capital infusions, coupled with upstream reforms and targets to double natural gas production, directly benefit integrated oil and gas players like ONGC and RIL by funding exploration, development activities, and expanding gas infrastructure. This creates significant opportunities for revenue growth and market penetration in both oil and gas segments.

forces.title: Domestic refining capacity expansion to meet surging demand.
forces.description: India's refining capacity is undergoing significant expansion, aiming to increase from 258.12 MMTPA (FY25) to 310 MMTPA by 2030, with long-term plans for 400-450 MMTPA. Integrated OMCs (IOC, BPCL, HPCL) and private players (RIL) are at the forefront of this growth, supported by high utilization rates (109% in FY24-25) and increasing domestic demand for petroleum products. This expansion ensures robust downstream operations and contributes to India's energy security, boosting profitability for integrated firms.

forces.title: OMC margin compression due to crude price hikes and retail price freezes.
forces.description: Integrated Indian OMCs face cyclical pressure when crude oil prices surge (e.g., above $100/bbl) while domestic retail prices for petrol and diesel remain fixed or under government control. This dynamic severely compresses marketing margins, often leading to losses from retail operations that can offset gains from refining. Excise duty adjustments by the government can partially mitigate this, but the inherent structure of fixed retail prices against volatile input costs remains a significant cyclical profitability challenge for OMCs.

forces.title: AI and digital transformation as a strategic imperative for financial performance.
forces.description: The oil and gas sector is undergoing a structural shift towards digital transformation, with AI becoming central to finance strategy. EY estimates that scaled digital operations can unlock US$1.6 trillion to US$2.5 trillion in value over the next decade by optimizing cash cycles, reducing operational inefficiencies, and enhancing decision-making. Integrated companies must adopt AI-driven solutions for credit-to-cash excellence, order smoothing, and platform integration to improve liquidity, fund energy transition investments, and gain a competitive edge in volatile markets.

forces.title: Unwinding of Russian crude discounts impacting refining margins.
forces.description: Integrated OMCs' Gross Refining Margins (GRMs), which benefited significantly from discounted Russian crude (at one point 36% of imports), are expected to moderate. New US sanctions and trade agreements compel Indian refiners to diversify crude sourcing to other regions, leading to a projected increase in the weighted average cost of crude oil by US$1.5-2.0 per barrel. This unwinding directly compresses the GRM premium enjoyed by Indian refiners, necessitating strategic adjustments to maintain profitability in their refining segments.

forces.title: Integrated refining-petrochemicals strategy driving value creation.
forces.description: Indian integrated refiners are increasingly focusing on deeper integration with petrochemicals to enhance profitability and diversify their product mix. Companies like IndianOil aim to significantly increase their Petrochemical Intensity Index (PII) by 2030, supported by a national capex push of US$37 billion. This strategy allows for optimized feedstock utilization, higher-value product output, and resilience against fluctuations in fuel demand, creating a structural tailwind for integrated players by leveraging their refining assets more effectively.

forces.title: Energy transition driving diversification into green fuels and renewables.
forces.description: India's energy transition goals are prompting integrated oil and gas companies to diversify their portfolios into green energy. Examples include IOCL investing in a green hydrogen plant at its Panipat refinery and ONGC acquiring renewable energy assets. This strategic pivot addresses decarbonization targets, creates new revenue streams, and positions integrated players for a future where bio-blends, natural gas, and cleaner fuels play a larger role. Such diversification hedges against long-term fossil fuel demand risks.

forces.title: Slow, costly, and competitive exploration environment.
forces.description: Ramping up exploration for hydrocarbon resources is becoming slower, costlier, riskier, and more competitive than expected, despite resilient demand. The industry faces a decade-long deprioritization of exploration, leading to smaller, less experienced teams and increasing geological challenges. Unlike past cycles, there's a lack of step-change technology advancements to improve success rates. This makes building high-quality exploration capabilities a critical differentiator, but failure risks escalating premiums for resource acquisition and fundamental risk for integrated companies without strong balance sheets.

viewpoints.title: Integrated oil and gas sector faces mounting pressure and high uncertainty.
viewpoints.description: The oil and gas sector is operating under significant pressure and market uncertainty, exacerbated by geopolitical disruptions. To succeed in this volatile environment in 2026 and beyond, integrated oil and gas companies must concentrate on strengthening core fundamentals: portfolio quality, capital efficiency, robust cash flow generation, and advanced organizational capabilities. This requires a disciplined focus on exploration, M&A strategies, project execution, efficient operations, and leveraging AI to navigate disruptions and ensure long-term value creation.

viewpoints.title: Fossil fuel demand remains resilient, especially in India and China.
viewpoints.description: Despite global decarbonization efforts, fossil fuels are projected to maintain a significant share of the total energy supply, particularly growing under current dynamics and divergent pathways scenarios. This indicates a persistent demand for integrated oil and gas products. While coal use may decline globally, its role in key regions like India and China remains substantial, and oil demand is not expected to significantly decrease in the near to medium term, securing the market for integrated players.

viewpoints.title: India's integrated oil and gas sector poised for significant growth and investment.
viewpoints.description: India's integrated oil and gas sector is experiencing robust growth, driven by increasing energy demand and strategic government investments. The country's refining capacity is set to expand significantly, with plans to double it by 2030 and increase it further by 2040. Substantial investments are also planned for exploration and production, petrochemicals, and gas pipeline networks. This supportive environment positions integrated players like ONGC, RIL, and major OMCs for sustained expansion across their value chains.

viewpoints.title: OMCs' profitability highly sensitive to crude prices and excise duty changes.
viewpoints.description: Indian Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), which operate integrated refining and retail businesses, face significant profitability pressures from volatile crude oil prices and government excise duty policies. While their Gross Refining Margins (GRMs) can improve with higher product cracks, their predominantly domestic retail operations incur substantial losses when crude prices rise but retail prices remain frozen. Recent excise duty cuts have helped OMCs manage break-even points, highlighting the delicate balance between refining gains and marketing losses, heavily influenced by state intervention.

viewpoints.title: AI adoption is critical for integrated O&G financial resilience and liquidity.
viewpoints.description: Integrated oil and gas companies are in a liquidity paradox, needing to fund massive energy transition investments while facing squeezed cash flows from crude volatility. Traditional funding is tightening, making internal liquidity crucial. EY projects digital transformation, particularly AI-driven working capital management, can unlock trillions in value by optimizing cash cycles, reducing disputes, and streamlining operations across the complex integrated value chain. Early AI adopters are transforming finance from a cost center into a strategic funding engine for the energy transition, securing resilience.

viewpoints.title: OMC margins face moderation as Russian crude discounts unwind.
viewpoints.description: Integrated Indian OMCs are expected to see a moderation in their Gross Refining Margins (GRMs) as geopolitical shifts, specifically US sanctions and a new India-US trade agreement, compel them to reduce discounted Russian crude oil imports. This will lead to a higher weighted average cost for crude sourcing. While marketing margins are anticipated to improve in the near term due to stable retail fuel prices, the overall outlook for GRMs is a shift from recent peaks to more moderate, albeit still healthy, levels, conditional on benign global crude prices.

viewpoints.title: India's integrated energy sector balancing fossil growth and green transition.
viewpoints.description: India's integrated oil and gas sector is navigating a complex 'energy balancing act,' where fossil fuel consumption and production are projected to increase alongside significant renewable energy expansion. This reflects a pragmatic approach to support economic growth and energy access while pursuing long-term climate ambitions. The refining industry is transforming with capacity expansions and petrochemical integration, indicating continued reliance on traditional fuels while preparing for a future with bio-blends and cleaner alternatives. However, high import dependency poses strategic risks.

viewpoints.title: Oil demand resilience supports continued fossil fuel investment for integrated players.
viewpoints.description: Integrated oil and gas executives globally largely anticipate that fossil fuel demand will continue to rise for at least the next decade, with peak oil demand expected in 2035 or later. This conviction supports ongoing capital investments in traditional hydrocarbon technologies. The outlook varies regionally, reflecting differing natural assets and energy security priorities. While some companies pull back from transition investments, those already heavily invested are staying the course, indicating a sustained focus on both traditional and select new energy ventures for integrated companies.

demand_drivers.description: These factors are expected to drive soaring demand for petrochemicals in India over the coming decades.

new_opportunities.description: India's ambition to become a major global supplier of petrochemicals, especially as integrated players like RIL enhance petrochemical intensity.

market_sizing.methodology: Planned capital expenditure to boost petrochemicals capacity, aiming for India to supply one-third of global capacity additions.

demand_drivers.driver: Energy security and reduced import dependency
demand_drivers.description: Significant investments are aimed at boosting domestic production to counter India's heavy reliance on crude oil imports.

new_opportunities.description: The substantial investment provides opportunities for integrated oil and gas companies (e.g., ONGC, RIL) to expand their upstream operations and improve domestic output.

market_sizing.methodology: Strategic investment plan by the Indian government for enhancing energy security through upstream reforms and wider crude sourcing.

demand_drivers.description: Internal liquidity unlocked by digital transformation is crucial for integrated O&G companies to fund decarbonization and other strategic initiatives amidst tightening traditional funding sources.
Faster demand shifts, geopolitical shocks, and algorithmic trading are compressing commodity cycles, requiring quicker responses and proactive financial management enabled by digital tools.

pnl_drivers.description: Predictive dispute prevention and automated collections can reduce Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) by 5 to 10 days, improving cash flow.
Digital optimization allows companies to collect cash faster than they pay it out, enhancing financial liquidity.
Automated reconciliation and validation can reduce revenue locked in disputes from 10-20% to below 2% of Accounts Receivables.

new_opportunities.description: Deploying predictive, autonomous cash orchestration to optimize credit-to-cash processes, order smoothing, customer experience, and platform integration.

market_sizing.methodology: EY's assessment of scaled digital operations (AI, sensors, cloud, autonomy) unlocking value across the oil and gas ecosystem. This represents combined operational efficiency gains, avoided losses, increased production, sustainability benefits, and improved decision-making.

demand_drivers.description: India's status as the world's fourth-largest economy with continued growth drives significant energy consumption across sectors.

demand_drivers.driver: Growth in mobility and transport fuel demand
demand_drivers.description: Increasing personal vehicle ownership, logistics, and freight activity contribute to rising petrol and diesel consumption.

market_sizing.methodology: Projection based on India's growth story and continued reliance on traditional energy sources despite energy transition efforts.

demand_drivers.description: India is the world’s third-largest consumer of oil, and primary energy demand is expected to nearly double by 2040. Refinery products like petrol and diesel are seeing increased consumption.
Rapid economic growth and urbanization in India are driving higher demand for petroleum products and petrochemicals.

market_sizing.methodology: India's refining capacity expansion target. Current capacity is 258.12 MMTPA (FY25).
